(Fayetteville, North Carolina) | college = [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]] (2016–2017) | draft_year = 2017 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 9 | draft_team = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | career_start = 2017 | years1 = {{nbay|2017|start}}–{{nbay|2018|end}} | team1 = [[Dallas Mavericks]] | years2 = {{nbay|2018|end}}–{{nbay|2020|end}} | team2 = [[New York Knicks]] | years3 = {{nbay|2020|end}} | team3 = [[Detroit Pistons]] | years4 = {{nbay|2021|full=y}} | team4 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | years5 = {{nbay|2022|full=y}} | team5 = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | years6 = {{nbay|2023|full=y}} | team6 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years7 = 2025 | team7 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | years8 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2025–2026]] | team8 = [[Wisconsin Herd]] | highlights = * [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]] ({{nbay|2017|end}}) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]] (2017) * Second-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2017) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman team (2017) | team9 = [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] | years9 = [[2025–26 NBA G League season|2026]]–present }} '''Dennis Cliff Smith Jr.''' (born November 25, 1997) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Sioux Falls Skyforce]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State Wolfpack]] and earned second-team all-conference honors in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC) as a freshman as well as ACC Rookie of the Year. Smith was selected ninth overall in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Smith spent two seasons in Dallas before being traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in January 2019. He was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in February 2021 and later joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as a free agent in September of the same year. He was waived by the Blazers in February 2022 after suffering a right elbow injury and signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]] in the 2022 off-season. He signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in July 2023. ==High school career== Smith attended [[Trinity Christian School (Fayetteville, North Carolina)|Trinity Christian School]] in [[Fayetteville, North Carolina]].{{cite web|title=Dennis Smith, Jr.|url=https://gopack.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=3935&path=mbball|website=GoPack.com.com|access-date=November 6, 2018}} During his first year at Trinity Christian in 2013, Smith came off the bench on the varsity basketball team, where he averaged 9.2 points and 3.0 assist per game.{{cite web|first=Harrison|last=Malkin|title=How Dennis Smith Jr rose from a bench warmer to a 5-star recruit|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2015/7/21/8923777/dennis-smith-jr-recruiting-duke-north-carolina-nc-state-louisville|work=[[SB Nation]]|date=July 21, 2015|access-date=August 14, 2023}} On December 28, 2013, Smith scored 41 points in an 82–73 win over Homeschool Christian Youth Association and future NBA player [[Justin Jackson (basketball, born 1995)|Justin Jackson]].{{cite web|first=Brett|last=Strelow|title=Dennis Smith Jr, Trinity Christian outduel UNC recruit Justin Jackson and HCYA|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/916dcaca-6fcb-11e3-b73b-001a4bcf6878.html|work=The Fayetteville Observer|date=December 28, 2013|access-date=February 8, 2020}}{{Dead link|date=March 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }} As a sophomore, Smith and Trinity Christian defeated Greenfield by one point to win the 2014 NCISAA 1-A State Championship; Smith scored 21 points and was named MVP.{{cite web|first=Nick|last=Stevens|title=Fayetteville's Dennis Smith Jr offered by Wake Forest|url=https://www.highschoolot.com/fayetteville-s-dennis-smith-offered-by-wake-forest/13647548/|work=High School OT|date=May 15, 2014|access-date=February 9, 2020}} During the season, Smith averaged, 17.6 [[points per game]] and 9.3 [[Assist (basketball)|assists]], 6.9 rebounds and 2.4 steals per game. After the conclusion of his sophomore season, Smith participated in the NBPA Top 100 Camp on June 19, 2014, at [[John Paul Jones Arena]] in [[Charlottesville, Virginia|Virginia]].{{cite news|url= https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/nbpa-top-100-camp-seven-takeaways-plus-top-performers/|title=NBPA top 100 camp: Seven takeaways, plus top performers|work=cbssports.com|access-date=June 20, 2014}} Smith also competed in the 2014 Adidas Nations.{{Cite news|url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/team-lillard-adidas-nations-championship/|title=Team Lillard wins Adidas Nations Championship|work=www.slamonline.com|access-date=August 6, 2014}} In his junior year, Smith and Trinity Christian played in the 2014–2015 High School OT Holiday Invitational Tournament at [[Broughton High School (North Carolina)|Broughton High School]] in [[Raleigh, North Carolina|Raleigh]]. On December 26, 2014, Smith scored 23 points to help Trinity defeat [[Ravenscroft School]] (83–60).{{Cite news|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2014/high-school-ot-holiday-invitational-smith-shines-in-walls-shoes|title=High School OT Holiday Invitational: Smith shines in Wall's shoes|work=www.usatidayhss.com|access-date=December 26, 2014}} On December 29, 2014, Smith went head to head with an [[Orangeville Prep]] that featured future NBA players [[Jamal Murray]] and [[Thon Maker]]. Smith scored 38 points in a losing effort as Trinity Christian lost (79–75) in the semi-finals.{{Cite news|url= https://www.highschoolot.com/maker-orangeville-win-battle-of-superstars-over-smith-trinity/14315934/?version=amp|title=Maker, Orangeville win battle of superstars over Smith, Trinity|publisher=High School OT|date=December 30, 2014|access-date=December 31, 2014}} On January 15, 2015, he scored 25 points in a 65–54 victory over [[James B. Dudley High School|Dudley High School]],{{Cite web|url=https://www.greensboro.com/sports/high-school/smith-jr-lets-his-play-do-talking-in-mlk-day/article_257ff934-a05b-11e4-8f5e-1794aae2aab7.html|title=Smith Jr lets his play do all the talking in MLK Day Scholastic Classic|last=Sirea|first=Joe|date=January 15, 2015|publisher=News & Record|access-date=February 9, 2020}} and on February 2, 2015, he scored 17 points to defeat Cape Fear Christian Academy in the NCISAA 1-A quarterfinals. On February 11, 2015, in the last game of the season, Smith scored 33 points in a (90–58) loss to [[Word of God Christian Academy]] in the NCISAA 1-A Semi-finals. On the season, Smith averaged 22.2 [[points per game]], 7.1 assists, 5.1 [[rebounds per game]] and 3 steals, while leading the Crusaders to a (23–10) overall record.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2015/7/21/8923777/dennis-smith-jr-recruiting-duke-north-carolina-nc-state-louisville|title=How Dennis Smith Jr rose from a bench warmer to five-star recruit|work=sbnation.com|access-date=July 21, 2015}} In 2015, he was named the [[Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year]] for North Carolina.[http://www.fayobserver.com/sports/20150320/trinity-christians-dennis-smith-jr-named-nc-gatorade-basketball-player-of-year Trinity Christian's Dennis Smith Jr. named N.C. Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year]{{cite web|url=http://www.foxsports.com/college-basketball/story/dennis-smith-jr-is-110-percent-healthy-and-ready-to-lead-nc-state-to-a-big-season-080316|title=Dennis Smith Jr. is '110 percent' healthy, ready to lead NC State to a big season|first=2016 at 1:45p|last=ET|date=August 3, 2016|work=Fox Sports|access-date=January 15, 2019}} Smith received surgery weeks later after the injury. Before the injury, in the summer of 2015, Smith competed on the [[Adidas]] Uprising Circuit for the [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] team, Team Loaded North Carolina (NC), alongside future NBA player [[Bam Adebayo]]. He led his team to victory in the Adidas Uprising Gauntlet Championship.{{Cite web|url=http://ballislife.com/dennissmith-bamadebayo-adidas-championship/|title=Dennis Smith & Bam Adebayo Lead Staked Team Loaded to Adidas Championship|last=Wellman|first=Webb|date=May 1, 2015|publisher=Ballislife|access-date=February 8, 2020}} Smith averaged 16.2 points, 4.8 rebounds and 6.9 assists in 11 games on the circuit.{{Cite news|url=http://www.fayobserver.com/598bce94-26be-11e5-9c5d-3f1b028ec345.html|title=Dennis Smith, Team Loaded conclude play at Adidas Uprising Gauntlet Finale|last=Strelow|first=Bret|date=July 10, 2015|work=fayobserver.com|access-date=April 25, 2017}} On July 27, 2015, in a televised game on [[ESPNU]], Smith recorded 29 points, 10 rebounds and 8 assists in a 78–77 win over [[Kyle Guy]] and Indiana Elite.{{Cite web|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/2015/07/27/dennis-smith-jr-team-loaded/22277575007/|title=Dennis Smith Jr, Team Loaded bounce back from semifinal loss, ends adidas Uprising event in strong fashion|last=Strelow|first=Bret|date=July 27, 2015|website=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]|access-date=August 14, 2023}} On August 10, 2015, while competing in an Adidas Nations event, Smith [[Anterior cruciate ligament injury|tore his ACL]], but did not feel any serious pain or swelling in his knee. During surgery, Smith's doctors found that he had an extra ACL. He was originally ruled out for his entire senior season of high school but in between two weeks and two months, he claimed that he had become more explosive, with his vertical increasing by 8 inches.{{Cite news|url=http://www.maxpreps.com/m/article.aspx?articleid=67043d04-8e5a-4e1d-9924-11fba6e1d4d4|title=No.1 Class of 2016 point guard Dennis Smith Jr suffers torn Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]], [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] and [[Kentucky Wildcats men's bball = yes }} ==College career== In December 2015, Smith decided to [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] and graduate early from Trinity Christian School and in January 2016 he enrolled at [[North Carolina State University]].{{cite news|first=John|last=Marshall|title=Duke recruit Bagley raises issue of 'reclassification'|date=August 19, 2017|work=Austin American-Statesman|url=https://www.statesman.com/story/news/2017/08/19/duke-recruit-bagley-raises-issue-of-reclassification/10378356007/|access-date=May 30, 2022}} He decided to take the opportunity to get an early start on his first year by attending classes and rehabbing from his injury with the NC State medical staff before the start of the [[2016–17 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2016–17 season]].{{Cite news|url=http://theacc.com/news/2016/12/30/5865fa1be4b02fca581ce80a_131480916700447096.aspx?path=mbball|title=Freshman Focus: Dennis Smith Jr|work=TheACC.com|access-date=December 30, 2016}} Smith began his freshman season playing in two exhibition games against [[Lynn University]] and [[Barton College]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article113187353.html|title=Defense lifts NC State to 112–60 rout of Barton|last=Giglo|first=Joe|date=November 7, 2016|access-date=January 26, 2017|via=newsobserver.com}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article112441112.html|title=Smith leads NC State to preseason rout of lynn|last=Giglo|first=Joe|date=November 3, 2016|access-date=January 26, 2017|via=newsobserver.com}} In his debut for the Wolfpack, Smith played 36 minutes and dished out five assists in an 81–79 victory against [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball|Georgia Southern]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/nc-state/article114302978.html|title=Just the beginning for NC State, Smith in Rocky debut – decock|last=Decock|first=Luke|date=November 11, 2016|access-date=January 26, 2017|via=newsobserver.com}} On November 21, 2016, Smith recorded a then-career-high 24 points to go along with 8 assists, defeating [[Saint Joseph's Hawks men's basketball|Saint Joseph's University]], 73–63, in the [[Paradise Jam tournament]]. On November 26, 2016, he scored a season-high 30 points, grabbed 6 rebounds and tallied 7 assists to help NC State defeat [[Loyola Ramblers men's basketball|Loyola University Chicago]].{{Cite news|url= https://gopack.com/news/2016/11/26/mens-basketball-wolfpack-downs-loyola-chicago-79-77.aspx|title=Wolfpack Downs Loyola Chicago 79-77|work=www.gopack.com|access-date=November 26, 2016}} On December 15, 2016, Smith recorded 22 points and 6 assists, leading NC State in a win over [[Appalachian State Mountaineers men's basketball|Appalachian State]]. On December 19, 2016, Smith earned ACC Freshman of the Week honors.{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2016/12/19/585832a0e4b04afe619b133c_131480917251604809.aspx|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Announces Basketball Players of the Week|date=December 19, 2016 |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=December 19, 2016}} On January 4, 2017, Smith recorded a triple-double—27 points, 11 rebounds and 11 assists—in a win against the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]], making him and [[Julius Hodge]] the only two NC State players to achieve this feat.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915358|title=Smith leads NC State past No.21 Virginia Tech 104-78|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=January 5, 2017}} On January 23, 2017, Smith scored a new career high with 32 points and 6 assists in an 84–82 victory against the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]], leading NC State to its first win at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] since 1995.{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915396|title=Smith, NC State stun No.17 Duke 84-82|website=ESPN.com|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=January 23, 2017}} Smith recorded his second triple-double—13 points, 15 assists and 11 rebounds—of the season on February 1 in a losing effort to [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]]. He is the only player in [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] history to have recorded two triple-doubles against league opponents.[http://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/dennis-smith-sets-acc-triple-double-record-but-nc-state-still-loses-things-to-know/ "Dennis Smith sets ACC triple-double record – but NC State still loses: Things to know."] CBSSports.com. N.p., February 2, 2017. Web. February 16, 2017. On February 7, 2017, Smith earned his second ACC rookie of the week honor{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2017/2/6/5898d1eee4b0a19b0eb20798_131480913369230793.aspx?path=mbball|title=Atlantic Coast Conference Announces Basketball Players of the Week|date=February 6, 2017 |publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|access-date=February 7, 2017}} On February 21, 2017, Smith scored 18 points in a 71–69 win against [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400915456|title=Wolfpack sting Georgia Tech, end 7 game slide|date=February 21, 2017|website=ESPN.com|access-date=February 21, 2017}} On March 5, 2017, Smith was named [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]].{{Cite news|url=https://gopack.com/news/2017/3/5/mens-basketball-dennis-smith-jr-named-acc-freshman-of-the-year.aspx|title=Dennis Smith named ACC Freshman of the Year|date=March 5, 2017|publisher=NC State Athletics|access-date=March 5, 2017}} Smith was additionally named to both Second team All-ACC and ACC All-Freshman teams.{{Cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2017/3/5/58bc7714e4b0af375f7cb2ea_131480910878223641.aspx?path=mbball|title=ACC Announces All-Conference Team, Postseason Awards|publisher=[[Atlantic Coast Conference]]|website=TheACC.com|date=March 5, 2017|access-date=February 9, 2020}} In 32 games for NC State in 2016–17, Smith averaged 18.1 points, 6.2 assists and 1.9 steals per game. After his freshman season, Smith announced his intention to forgo his final three years of collegiate eligibility and enter the [[2017 NBA draft]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2017/03/28/nc-state-freshman-guard-dennis-smith-jr-declares-for-nba/99731798/|title=NC State freshman guard Dennis Smith Jr declares for NBA Draft|work=www.usatoday.com|access-date=March 28, 2017}} His illegal recruitment where he was paid by NC State coaches led to NCAA sanctions.{{Cite news |date=20 December 2021 |title=NCAA violations place NC State basketball on probation, revoke 1 scholarship |url=https://abc11.com/nc-state-basketball-dennis-smith-ncaa-violations-jr/11361961/ |work=[[WTVD-TV]]}} ==Professional career== ===Dallas Mavericks (2017–2019)=== Smith was selected with the ninth overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]] by the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-pick-2017-nba-draft/|title=Mavericks select Dennis Smith Jr. with ninth overall pick in 2017 NBA Draft|website=mavs.com|date=June 22, 2017|access-date=June 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171019112047/https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-pick-2017-nba-draft/|archive-date=October 19, 2017|url-status=dead}} On July 5, 2017, he signed his rookie contract.{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-dennis-smith-jr/|title=Mavs sign first-round pick Dennis Smith Jr.|website=mavs.com|date=July 5, 2017|access-date=July 5, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170706021643/https://www.mavs.com/mavs-sign-dennis-smith-jr/|archive-date=July 6, 2017|url-status=dead}} While Smith would be out of action during the [[2017 NBA Summer League]] in Orlando, he would return to action just in time for the event in Las Vegas. During the six games he played with the Mavericks out in Las Vegas, Smith recorded 17.3 points, 4.8 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 2.2 steals per game in under 25.9 minutes of action, which earned him All-Summer League first-team honors.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2017-all-nba-summer-league-teams-lakers-rookie-lonzo-ball-earns-mvp-honors/|title=2017 All-NBA Summer League teams: Lakers rookie Lonzo Ball earns MVP honors|website=cbssports.com|date=July 18, 2017|access-date=July 18, 2017}} On October 18, 2017, Smith made his debut in the Mavericks' season opener, a 117–111 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]], where he scored 16 points and had 10 assists.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974705|title=Hawks, Schroder spoil Smith's debut, top Mavericks 117–111|publisher=ESPN|date=October 18, 2017|access-date=October 18, 2017}} On December 29, 2017, he recorded his first career triple-double with 21 points, 10 rebounds and 10 assists in a 128–120 win over the [[New Orleans Pelicans]]. He was 5 of 7 from three-point range and 8 of 12 overall from the field. At 20 years, 34 days, Smith became the sixth-youngest player in NBA history to have a triple-double, behind [[Lonzo Ball]], [[Markelle Fultz]], [[Luka Dončić]] and [[LeBron James]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975271|title=Dennis Smith Jr. has triple-double, Mavs beat Pelicans|publisher=ESPN|date=December 29, 2017|access-date=December 29, 2017}} On May 22, 2018, he was named to the [[NBA All-Rookie Team|NBA All-Rookie Second Team]].{{cite news|title=Donovan Mitchell, Ben Simmons lead 2017–18 NBA All-Rookie first team|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2018/05/22/all-rookie-teams-release-2017-18-season|access-date=May 22, 2018|publisher=National Basketball Association|date=May 22, 2018}} On October 28, 2018, Smith scored 27 points, alongside three assists and two blocks, in a 113–104 loss to the [[Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web |title=Utah Jazz vs Dallas Mavericks Oct 28, 2018 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800084 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On January 30, 2019, in his last game before being traded, Smith recorded his second career triple-double with 13 points, ten rebounds and a career-high 15 assists in a 114–90 win over the [[New York Knicks]], the team he would get traded to.{{Cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks vs New York Knicks Jan 30, 2019 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800758 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===New York Knicks (2019–2021)=== [[File:Dennis Smith Jr (cropped).jpg|thumb|Smith with the [[New York Knicks]] in 2020]] On January 31, 2019, Smith was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] along with [[DeAndre Jordan]], [[Wesley Matthews]] and two future first-round draft picks in exchange for [[Kristaps Porziņģis]], [[Tim Hardaway Jr.]], [[Trey Burke]] and [[Courtney Lee]].{{cite web|title=Knicks Acquire Dennis Smith Jr., Deandre Jordan, Wesley Matthews, and Two Future First round Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-dennis-smith-jr-deandre-jordan-wesley-matthews-from-dallas|website=NBA.com|date=January 31, 2019|access-date=January 16, 2025}} Summary|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800817|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 21, 2023}} On April 9, Smith recorded 25 points and five assists in a 96–86 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|title=Knicks top Bulls 96–86, avoid new franchise low for wins|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071886|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April 9, 2019}} On December 1, 2019, Smith scored a season-high 17 points, alongside seven assists and two blocks, in a 113–104 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web|title=TATUM, BROWN LEAD CELTICS' RALLY PAST KNICKS|url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900285|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 21, 2023}} On February 1, 2021, Smith was assigned to the [[Westchester Knicks]], the affiliate of New York in the [[NBA G League]].{{cite tweet|title=@nyknicks Sign Tyler Hall|number=1356260113607225347|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=February 1, 2021|access-date=January 16, 2025}}{{cite 2021|access-date=February 4, 2021}} He reportedly requested to be sent down to the team in order to get more playing time; however, he never played a game in the G League for the Knicks.{{cite web|title=Knicks Rumors: Dennis Smith Jr. Requests to Play in G League Bubble|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2929020-knicks-rumors-dennis-smith-jr-requests-to-play-in-g-league-bubble|website=BleacherReport.com|access-date=February 21, 2023}} During the 2020–21 season, Smith only played three games for the Knicks at the NBA level. ===Detroit Pistons (2021)=== On February 8, 2021, Smith was traded, alongside a future second-round pick, to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Derrick Rose]].{{cite web |title=Knicks Acquire Derrick Rose |url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/front-office-news/knicks-acquire-derrick-rose |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 8, 2021 |date=February 8, 2021}}{{cite web |title=Detroit Pistons Acquire Guard Dennis Smith Jr. and a Future Second-Round Pick From New York Knicks In Exchange For Derrick Rose.|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-acquire-guard-dennis-smith-jr-and-future-second-round-pick-new-york-knicks |website=NBA.com |access-date=February 8, 2021 |date=February 8, 2021}} Smith made his Pistons debut three days later, recording four points and two rebounds in a 111–95 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{Cite web |title=PACERS SNAP 4-GAME SKID WITH 111-95 WIN OVER PISTONS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000391 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On February 26, he scored a season-high 17 points, alongside six assists, in a 110–107 loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]].{{Cite web |title=KINGS SNAP SKID, TOP PISTONS 110-107 IN STRANGE FINISH |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000504 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On March 3, Smith recorded his third career triple-double with ten points, eleven assists and a career-high twelve rebounds in a 129–105 win over the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{Cite web |title=ELLINGTON, BACKUPS HELP PISTONS BEAT DEPLETED RAPTORS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000539 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} ===Portland Trail Blazers (2021–2022)=== On September 23, 2021, Smith signed with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers announce Training Camp roster|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-announce-training-camp-roster-0|date=September 23, 2021|website=NBA.com|accessdate=September 23, 2021}} He made his Trail Blazers debut on October 23, recording two points, two rebounds and five assists in a 134–105 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=MCCOLLUM HELPS BLAZERS ROUT SUNS FOR FIRST WIN OF SEASON |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100033 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On December 4, Smith scored a season-high 21 points, alongside four rebounds, six assists and three steals, in a 145–117 loss to the [[Boston Celtics]].{{Cite web |title=CELTICS START FAST, ROUT TRAIL BLAZERS 145-117 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022100347 |access-date=February 21, 2023 |website=NBA.com}} On February 16, 2022, he was diagnosed with a high-grade partial tear of the [[ulnar collateral ligament]] (UCL) in his right elbow, and was subsequently ruled out for three-to-four weeks.{{Cite web |title=DENNIS SMITH JR. INJURY UPDATE |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/dennis-smith-jr-injury-update |access-date=February 21, 2022 |website=Portland Trail Blazers}} On February 21, Smith was waived by the Trail Blazers.{{Cite web |title=TRAIL BLAZERS SIGN TRENDON WATFORD TO STANDARD NBA CONTRACT |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/trail-blazers-sign-trendon-watford-standard-nba-contract |access-date=February 21, 2022 |website=NBA}} He remained unsigned throughout the remainder of the 2021–22 season. ===Charlotte Hornets (2022–2023)=== After being waived by Portland, Smith considered attempting to sign with an [[National Football League|NFL]] team as a defensive back rather than playing basketball overseas.{{Cite web |title=Dennis Smith Jr. says he was trying to make the NFL before Hornets signed him |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/dennis-smith-jr-says-he-was-trying-to-make-the-nfl-before-hornets-signed-him/ |access-date=2023-04-01 |website=CBSSports.com |date=October 27, 2022 |language=en}} However, Smith was invited to the Charlotte Hornets' preseason camp. On September 23, 2022, Smith signed with his hometown team, the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite web|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Free Agent Dennis Smith Jr. |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-sign-free-agent-dennis-smith-jr |date=September 23, 2022 |website=NBA.com |accessdate=September 23, 2022}} On October 19, he made his Hornets debut, recording 12 points, two rebounds, four assists, two blocks and two steals in a 129–102 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468026|title=Rozier scores 24 as Hornets rout youthful Spurs|date=October 19, 2022|website=[[ESPN]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=October 30, 2022}} On October 23, Smith recorded 18 points and six assists in a 126–109 victory against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401468193|title=Oubre, Richards power Hornets to 126-109 win over Hawks|date=October 23, 2022|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=October 30, 2022}} ===Brooklyn Nets (2023–2024)=== [[File:Dennis Smith Jr (cropped).png|thumb|right|Smith with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in 2024]] On July 8, 2023, Smith signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-dennis-smith-jr|title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Dennis Smith Jr.|date=July 8, 2023|website=NBA.com|access-date=July 9, 2023}} Smith made 56 appearances (including two starts) for the Nets, recording averages of 6.6 points, 2.9 rebounds, and 3.6 assists.{{Cite web|title=Dennis Smith Jr. 2023-24 Stats per He appeared in two Liga ACB games, averaging 1.5 points in 7.5 minutes, and two EuroLeague games where he averaged 4.0 points in 10.5 minutes.{{cite web |title=Dennis Smith Jr. International Stats 2025|website=dallasnews.com}} On November 17, Smith signed with the [[Wisconsin Herd]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{Cite web|title=WISCONSIN HERD ADDS DENNIS SMITH
